title: The Repeating Scratch
brief: At Meridian Microworks, a curved scratch appears on about 1 in 200 wafers after final clean. It has been seen for 3 months. Corrective action CA-77 says "handlers to take more care". You have 12 visit points to interview staff and reach a system cause.

actions.label: General condition of the area
actions.note: Nothing of note for the purpose of this visit.

actions.label: A staff member: anything else to mention
actions.note: The staff member has nothing further to add on this topic.

actions.label: Older records for this area
actions.note: The older records show nothing relevant to this visit.

actions.label: Notices and signs in the area
actions.note: The notices are current and not relevant to this visit.

evidence.text: CA-77 cause "handling", action "handlers to take more care", closed after 2 weeks with no check; scratches continued at the same rate.
evidence.whyItMatters: Corrective action must find and remove the cause and be checked.
evidence.missedExplanation: Check whether the problem stopped after closure.

evidence.text: Scratch map data: 41 of 43 scratches are at the same position near the notch, all on wafers from cassette slot 25.
evidence.whyItMatters: The pattern points to equipment, not people.

evidence.text: Technician: "Always the top slot, I think. I log every one."
evidence.whyItMatters: The technician reports issues and gives a lead.

evidence.text: Robot end effector R-3 has a worn pad on one finger; the pad is a non-standard part number EP-11X.
evidence.whyItMatters: Equipment must be maintained to achieve conformity.
evidence.missedExplanation: Look at the equipment that touches the product.

evidence.text: Robot maintenance record: pad inspection is scheduled every 4 weeks but last recorded 14 weeks ago.
evidence.whyItMatters: Planned maintenance must be done as scheduled.
evidence.missedExplanation: Compare planned and actual maintenance dates.

evidence.text: Maintenance: "We switched to a cheaper pad EP-11X 3 months ago when the usual one was out of stock. No trial." (note 5)
evidence.whyItMatters: Changes affecting production must be reviewed before use.
evidence.missedExplanation: Ask what changed when the problem began.

evidence.text: Robot calibration procedure has no step for the top slot height; slot 25 is 0.4 mm closer to the arm than others.
evidence.whyItMatters: Process settings must ensure conforming output in all conditions.

evidence.text: Spare parts record shows EP-11X was bought from the approved supplier.
evidence.whyItMatters: The supplier is approved; the gap is the change review.

evidence.text: Handler: "We load full cassettes with the tool and don't touch wafer faces." Observation confirms this.
evidence.missedExplanation: Conforming evidence that rules out handling.

evidence.text: One handler wears gloves of a different color, from an approved type list.
Scratch inspection method SI-2 is current and detects the scratch reliably.
evidence.whyItMatters: Detection works; prevention is the gap.

decisions.prompt: Which statement best describes the system cause?
options: An unreviewed change to pad EP-11X, missed pad maintenance, and no calibration step for slot 25 let the robot touch wafers in the top slot
Wafers from the supplier are fragile
Scratches are normal and should be accepted
decisions.rationale: The evidence points to equipment, maintenance, and change control.

containment: Stop using slot 25 on robot R-3 and inspect wafers from it until fixed
correction: Replace the worn pad with the standard part and recalibrate
cause: Unreviewed part substitution, missed maintenance, and no calibration step for the top slot
corrective: Route part substitutions through change control, add maintenance due alerts, and add slot 25 to calibration
effectiveness: Track scratches by slot for eight weeks, target zero at slot 25

debriefText.found: You followed the pattern to the robot.
debriefText.missed: Position patterns usually point to equipment.
debriefText.falseFinding: Approved gloves and normal hours were not causes.
